extracted.intended_audience: readers of Popular Science Monthly — educated general public and scientifically interested readers (including practicing scientists)
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizing and interpreting experimental investigations (here in hydrodynamics/electricity and in microbiology) for a general scientific audience, emphasizing apparatus, methods, results, and cautious inference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental confirmation against theoretical predictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Experimental results should correspond with prior mathematical calculations; experiments are valuable when they reproduce or confirm theoretical predictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bjerknes's experiments 'in every case corresponded with those which had previously been indicated to him by mathematical calculations.' Use experiments to test and corroborate theoretical models; discrepancies or matches are central to claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controlled variation of pulsation/oscillation phase to test interactions
rubrics_metrics.description: Vary the relative phases (synchronous vs opposite) of pulsating or oscillating bodies to observe attraction or repulsion and thereby test hypotheses about interactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use separate pumps/drums or independently driven pulsators so rhythms can be regulated; attraction when phases are the same, repulsion when opposite (as shown in Bjerknes's setups). Explicitly manipulate phase as an experimental variable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of different motion modalities (pulsation vs oscillation) and orientations
rubrics_metrics.description: Test phenomena using both volume-changing (pulsating) bodies and constant-volume oscillating bodies, and vary oscillation directions (horizontal/vertical) to explore different manifestations of the effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substitute spheres that oscillate horizontally or vertically; observe how configurations change attraction/repulsion and directive effects (e.g., turning around an axis). Vary geometry to map behavior comprehensively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of object properties (mass, buoyancy, material) to probe analogies
rubrics_metrics.description: Change physical properties of test objects (light cork vs heavier metal) to reveal different relative motions with the surrounding medium and thus different interaction behaviors (analogs of dia- and para-magnetism).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspend objects of differing density/ mass in the fluid and compare their oscillations relative to water; observe repulsion vs attraction and equatorial vs axial alignment (e.g., cork sets equatorially, metal axially).

rubrics_metrics.name: Visualization of field/force lines using tracer apparatus
rubrics_metrics.description: Map the pattern of disturbances (analogous to magnetic lines of force) by using a lightweight probe with a brush or tracer to record fluid vibrations on a surface.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mount a light sphere/cylinder on an elastic rod in the fluid with an attached brush to paint vibration lines on a glass plate above; compare resulting figures to iron filings patterns in magnetic fields (use concordant vs discordant pulsations and varying numbers of pulsators).

rubrics_metrics.name: Require independent confirmation before asserting theoretical conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Promulgated experimental conclusions, especially those that propose novel analogies or theoretical claims, should be regarded as provisional until further confirmation is obtained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article explicitly cautions that interesting conclusions from Bjerknes's experiments 'need to be further confirmed before a positive announcement of them can be justified.' Emphasize replication and independent verification before strong claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Microscopic identification and differential staining of suspected agent in lesions
rubrics_metrics.description: Locate and visually identify a consistent microorganism in diseased tissue using microscopy and a special dye that differentiates it from surrounding tissue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Koch 'found, in all cases, the tubercles infested with a minute, rod-shaped parasite, which, by means of a special dye, he differentiated from the surrounding tissue.' Demonstrating presence within lesions supports causation claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Isolation and prolonged cultivation of the suspected pathogen
rubrics_metrics.description: Grow the suspected organism in artificial nutritive media over successive generations to show it can propagate independently of host tissue or accompanying substances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Koch cultivated bacilli for many successive generations (months) in prepared media; repeated subculture producing pure generations helps rule out that disease depends on some other non-living 'virus' in the tissue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproduction of the disease by inoculating healthy hosts with the cultured organism
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduce the isolated/cultured organism into healthy animals and observe whether the original disease is reproduced, thereby supporting a causal link.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Koch inoculated guinea-pigs, rabbits, and other animals with cultured bacilli (from human or animal lungs) and reproduced tubercular disease; cross-species inoculation and consistent disease reproduction strengthen causal inference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of uninfected controls in infection experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: Include animals that are not inoculated (or are given inert/control material) to demonstrate that observed disease results from the inoculum and not from other causes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In Koch's experiments two uninfected guinea-pigs remained perfectly healthy while inoculated ones developed disease. Controls are essential to rule out spontaneous disease or environmental confounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test multiple routes of inoculation to examine infectivity pathways
rubrics_metrics.description: Deliver the suspect agent by different anatomical routes (e.g., abdominal injection, injection into aqueous humor) to test whether infection and disease follow across routes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Koch changed inoculation site from the abdomen to the eye's aqueous humor and still produced pulmonary tubercles. Demonstrating infectivity via multiple routes informs transmission hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine environmental growth requirements (e.g., temperature range)
rubrics_metrics.description: Characterize the organism's abiotic growth limits (such as minimum and maximum temperatures) to infer whether it can propagate outside a host.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Koch determined the tubercle-bacillus grows between 86°F and 104°F, concluding that animal warmth is necessary in temperate zones—such parameters affect environmental survival and epidemiological conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate environmental persistence and infectivity of expelled material
rubrics_metrics.description: Test whether material expectorated by diseased hosts (e.g., sputum) remains infective after drying and over time, to assess transmission risk via dust/air.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Koch showed dried sputum kept two, four, and eight weeks remained virulent when used to infect guinea-pigs, indicating grave danger from inhalation of dried infectious particles; such persistence experiments inform public-health measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-species and multiple-animal testing for generality
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform infection experiments across a variety of animal species to evaluate the breadth of host susceptibility and generality of findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Koch tested cats, rabbits, rats, mice, etc., and found consistent production of disease; broad testing increases confidence that the agent is the causal pathogen rather than species-specific artifact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thorough post-mortem examination and documentation of pathology
rubrics_metrics.description: After experimental endpoints, perform detailed necropsy/examination of organs to document presence, distribution, and severity of disease lesions attributed to the inoculum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Koch examined spleen, liver, lungs, etc., noting tubercles throughout infected animals; systematic pathological documentation is critical to link inoculation to disease phenotype.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cautious translation of experimental findings into public policy or moral prescriptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid enacting harsh or morally questionable public-health measures without robust experimental foundation; balance compassion with evidence-based actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tyndall argues against 'enact[ing] cruelty in the name of tenderness' and emphasizes that common sense will not permit premature or cruel policies. Experimental claims should guide humane, justified policy.
